The ADR must come first so reviewers can verify correctness bit-by-bit against the spec.

proposals.why_now: FASE-1 requires 'Loop de tick com a ordem canônica implementada' and market-order buy/sell spot. The canonical tick order from §7 is TRAVADO and must be implemented in a single readable location with a test that verifies the step order. This is the integration point between core, world, and domain and the last piece needed before the CLI replay tool and FASE-1 acceptance.

repository_assessment.current_state: Monorepo foundation is in place (npm workspaces, tsconfig, eslint, boundary gates, test infrastructure) from the pre-benchmark scaffolding. All 8 packages and 4 desktop sub-apps exist but every src/index.ts is an empty stub. No ADRs have been committed. No substantive implementation code has been accepted in 32 checkpoints (all show NO_ACCEPTED_CHANGES, internal_commit_count=0). Six consecutive tasks (TASK-0003 through TASK-0008) targeted the CanonicalEncoder; all were rejected — first for a non-enumerable property defect, then for incorrect task framing as an amendment to non-existent code.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: The canonical encoder (ADR-009) has never been successfully implemented and accepted. It is the mandatory prerequisite for all FASE-1 state hashing. The last review (TASK-0008-review-02) cited BLOCKER-0001 as blocking, but SPEC_BLOCKERS.md contains no registered blockers; that reference was an uncommitted implementation artifact. The correct next step is a fresh CanonicalEncoder implementation — not an amendment — that explicitly rejects non-enumerable own properties and captures compile evidence.
